- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer for volatility or adjust downward if sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion; allow 1–2% downward drift in forecast if no new bullish events.
- If multiple auction events occur in 5–7 days, model tends to overreact to supply shocks; dampen forecast growth by 1–3% per event unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to account for sentiment decay; apply exponential decay to sentiment weights (e.g., 0.95 per day) to smooth forecast bias.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after spike, model should not assume continuation; use 3–5 day moving average to anchor forecast if sentiment weakens.
